Adversity

ad-VER-si-tee · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Adversity is a difficult or unfortunate situation; hardship and suffering.

The biography spends its first three chapters on the adversity the inventor endured before a single one of his ideas ever worked.

Worked Example

The memoir describes how the family's years of adversity during the drought -- lost crops, lost income, and a burned-down barn -- only strengthened their bond.

Adversity is ongoing difficulty or misfortune -- the hard circumstances a person has to struggle through, not a single bad moment.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

hardship: severe suffering or difficulty

misfortune: bad luck; an unfortunate event

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

prosperity: the state of being successful and thriving

fortune: good luck; favorable circumstances

Where it sits · how severe the trouble is — inconvenience → adversity → calamity

inconvenience vs. adversity: An inconvenience is a minor annoyance or difficulty, far milder than the serious, ongoing struggle of adversity.

calamity vs. adversity: A calamity is an even more extreme, sudden disaster than ordinary adversity, often affecting many people at once.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — advers-

root — advers-: turned against, opposed (Latin adversus)

suffix — -ity

suffix — -ity: state of, quality of (Latin/French)

Put it together

Put it together: Adversity comes from Latin adversus ('turned against, opposed'), the same root behind the everyday word adverse, plus -ity -- 'the state of having circumstances turned against you.'

Use the root in a new word: adverse

Use the root in a new word: adverse: The pilot delayed takeoff because of adverse weather conditions moving into the area.
